messages:
micah: Heads-up — Helios just announced a per-tenant streaming API with built-in routing-by-cost. Sales flagged two pilots asking for "pin-to-tenant" routing. Need a product decision by EOD on whether we match parity or double down on our cost-aware controls.

sophia: Got the alert. Can you drop the link? I want to see their UX assumptions.

micah: https://twitter.com/heliosai/status/1711100000
Also sales notes: Acme + Nova are explicitly asking for per-tenant model pinning and firm fallback guarantees.

alex: Quick engineering sanity check: implementing full parity (hard reservations + console end-to-end) is nontrivial. Ballpark: infra effort ~3 sprints to avoid fragmentation + ~1 sprint console work.

jamal: @alex can you enumerate the top infra risks? Autoscaling impacts and KV cache isolation are the first that come to mind.

alex: Biggest risks: autoscaler unaware of hard reservations -> capacity silos and degraded utilization. KV cache isolation increases per-tenant memory footprint and OOM risk. Mitigations: soft reservations + eviction strategy, or dedicated pools per tier. Each has tradeoffs for cost and latency.

tara: What if MVP is a lightweight routing policy surface we can ship quickly: allow pinning behaviour via routing_policy flags but enforce soft reservations and deterministic fallback. That keeps dev work small and keeps our positioning around cost controls.

sophia: Agreed. Proposed launch acceptance criteria from product side:
- routing config that enables behavioral pinning (routing_policy) without silent OOMs or cross-tenant KV leaks
- 99th percentile latency for pinned routes within existing SLOs
- two pilot customers onboarded and billing validated
- console controls and docs for routing + fallback

micah: My recommendation: greenlight a 6-week spike to validate the config surface, autoscaler interactions, and billing implications. If the spike surfaces <2 sprints of follow-up infra work, move to full parity; otherwise ship the constrained routing controls as our differentiator.

alex: I'll scope the spike: prototype autoscaler behavior with soft reservations, a console mock for routing controls, KV isolation smoke tests, and e2e billing validation. Draft RFC at https://redwood.in/notes/233 (internal).

deploy-bot: ticket INF-8347 created: "per-tenant routing spike" (assignee: alex)

jamal: Security/controls note: tenant pinning to specific model binaries increases KMS scoping and audit requirements. Add KMS policy checks and audit hooks to spike scope.

tara: Customers also requested deterministic fallback behavior when the pinned model is overloaded. We should add explicit fallback_policy and a cost_threshold.

micah: Decision: greenlight the spike. Owners: alex (eng infra), tara (product), jamal (security), sophia (sales liaison). Checkpoint Thu 11:00. If spike shows <2 sprints follow-up, aim for full feature; else ship routing_policy + deterministic fallback as our cost/perf differentiator.

sophia: I'll loop in Acme and Nova, confirm their test cases and expected fallback semantics.

jamal: I'll draft KMS/audit requirements and enumerate potential compliance blockers.

alex: Posting RFC to #eng-runtime and will attach the initial spike plan by EOD. Example config sketch for the spike (API + console):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  pin_to_tenant: true
  fallback_model: "redwood-compact-v2"
  cost_threshold_usd_per_token: 0.0004
  eviction_policy: "age-based"
```

tara: Adding "fallback determinism" and "billing validation" to spike acceptance criteria.

micah: Final: checkpoint Thu 11:00. If anyone needs more context ping me or drop notes in the RFC thread. :rocket:
